evidence.paraphrase: After Dākṣāyaṇī’s death, Śiva withdraws; her rebirth serves him. Gods oppressed by Tāraka seek a son of Śiva and send Kāma, recalling Viṣṇu’s earlier gifts. Kāma shoots Śiva, whose recovered composure leads him to burn Kāma with his third eye; Gaurī leaves for penance.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Citrakarmā shapes Kāma’s ashes into a boy; Rudra’s gaze animates him. Addressing him as son, Citrakarmā teaches Śatarudriya worship. Śiva accepts the boy’s requests for half his opponent’s strength and arrow-based neutralization of hostile weapons, additionally granting sixty thousand years of rule. Brahmā’s utterance supplies the name Bhaṇḍa.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Śukra crowns Bhaṇḍa; Maya rebuilds Śoṇitapura. Royal gifts include Vijaya bow, protective umbrella, disease-averting chowries and indestructible crown. Eight assistants and four wives are listed. The asuras maintain Vedic rites and Śiva worship during sixty thousand years.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Viṣṇu sends his deluding Māyā with Viśvācī’s companions; Bhaṇḍa neglects worship. Nārada urges Indra to worship Parāśakti. Śukra warns Bhaṇḍa; Śrutavarmā notes the expired reign, while Bhīmakarmā trusts his combat boon and urges disruption.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Repeated attacks, including Vāyavya, fail against the regenerated divine wall. Indra’s gods offer their own flesh in a great sacrifice. Lalitā emerges with noose, goad, sugarcane bow and five arrows; her glance restores the mutilated gods.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: The gods praise Lalitā’s cosmic identity; Indra requests rescue. She promises personally to defeat Bhaṇḍa and restore the worlds. Devout recitation of this hymn receives blessings of virtue, learning, longevity, health and family prosperity.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Gods and attendants arrive; Viśvakarmā builds a city at Brahmā’s command. Considering a suitable coronation and spouse, Brahmā sees Śiva assume a beautiful form and names him Kāmeśvara. Lalitā and Kāmeśvara mutually desire each other; Brahmā requests their joint enthronement.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Lalitā insists on independence and a compatible husband; her thrown garland selects Kāmeśvara. Brahmā calls Viṣṇu her brother; Viṣṇu performs the marriage. Gods provide weapons and regalia. Brahmā’s Kusumākara chariot resists weapons, travels freely and removes afflictions through its fragrance.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: After the procession, Lalitā fulfills the assembly’s desires by her glance; Brahmā names her Kāmākṣī and Kāmeśvarī. Following ten thousand years of imperial life, Nārada recalls Bhaṇḍa’s threat. Gods return to their homes while continuing service through partial manifestations.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Lalitā’s campaign begins. Sampatkarī emerges from her goad and leads elephants on Kaṇakolāhala. Atitvaritavikrānti emerges from the noose, rides Aparājita and leads cavalry; her four hands hold noose, goad, cane and bridle. Daṇḍanāthā’s war preparation follows.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Daṇḍanāthā rides Vajraghoṣa with boar-faced troops. The text gives her twelve names, including Vārāhī, then Śyāmalā’s names, including Mantriṇī. Dhanurveda emerges from Śyāmalā’s parrot and gives Citrajīva and inexhaustible quivers. Yantriṇī and Tantriṇī attend her.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Lalitā proceeds on Śrīcakra, armed with goad, noose, sugarcane bow and five arrows, attended by Kāmeśvarī and other eternal powers. Hayagrīva supplies twenty-five epithets and benefits of their recitation.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Hayagrīva describes Lalitā’s Cakrarāja tiers, including Siddhis, eight mothers, Mudrās, successive yoginī groups and fifteen Nityās. Mantriṇī’s seven-tier Geyacakra houses allied powers, Bhairavas, protective deities and guardians; petitions reach Lalitā through Mantriṇī. Alternative maternal iconography is explicitly reported.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Kiricakra houses Daṇḍanāthā and supporting powers, including Jṛmbhiṇī, Mohinī, Stambhinī, Dhātunāthās, personified plough and pestle, guardians and vehicles. Surāsindhu’s prospective role is to refresh thirsty combatants. The witness calls this a five-step chariot but later mentions a sixth step.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Omens disturb Śūnyaka. Bhaṇḍa’s younger brothers Viśukra and Viṣaṅga advise him: Viśukra derides female opponents, while Viṣaṅga urges investigation and recalls earlier divine victories. Bhaṇḍa rejects the warning, boasts of his forces and named sons, and orders Kuṭilākṣa to fortify the city and send an advance force.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Bhaṇḍa sends Durmada; Kuṭilākṣa deploys Tālajaṅgha, Tālabhuja, Tālagrīva and Tālaketu at city gates. Sampatkarī fights Durmada on Raṇakolāhala. After Durmada strikes a crown jewel, her arrows pierce his chest and kill him; survivors flee.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Kuraṇḍa, Durmada’s elder brother, seeks revenge. The cavalry goddess asks Sampatkarī to yield the fight, then binds his army with multiplying nooses. Kuraṇḍa cuts her bowstring; she kills him with her goad, whose Pūtanās consume his forces. Survivors retreat.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Five generals deploy Sarpiṇī, whose destroyed snakes multiply while she survives. Lalitā’s palate-born Nakulī rides Garuḍa, creates mongooses from her teeth and dissolves Sarpiṇī with Gāruḍa. Enemy arrows rout her mongooses; Akṣīṇanākula renews the force. Nakulī kills Karaṅka and four colleagues. Śyāmalā makes her a satellite deity; she spares surviving messengers.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Kīkasā’s seven sons attack with a Sun-granted gaze that burns and immobilizes seen enemies and weapons. Lalitā summons Tiraskaraṇikā, Daṇḍanāthā’s guard. From Tamolipta she uses Mohana arrows and Andha to blind them; lost sight ends immobilization. She kills all seven, and the Śaktis destroy their army.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Before the origin account, Hayagrīva previews Bhaṇḍa’s domination: Viśukra emerges from his right shoulder, Viṣaṅga from his left; he also creates sister Dūminī. The three oppose gods, who flee their offices and families.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: After defeats, Bhaṇḍa orders Viṣaṅga and fifteen generals to attack Lalitā’s rear secretly, aiming to destroy the source of her powers. Dark equipment and silence conceal their approach. They reach Cakrarāja’s ninth tier and wound defenders with invisible Vipāṭas.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Kuṭilākṣa prevents the vanguard returning while Viṣaṅga breaks Lalitā’s fan. Nityās obtain her permission to intervene. Vahnivāsinī and Jvālāmālinī illuminate the attackers; the Nityās descend with Prāṇakodaṇḍas and fight for three watches.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: The Nityās kill the invading generals. Kāmeśvarī breaks Viṣaṅga’s armour; he escapes near dawn, destined for Daṇḍanāthā’s later attack. The Nityās refuse to pursue a fleeing warrior. Lalitā’s glance heals their wounds.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Daṇḍanāthā routs Kuṭilākṣa’s night force. She and Mantriṇī acknowledge inadequate rear protection and propose a guarded fire enclosure. Lalitā approves defence before offence. Jvālāmālinī becomes the enclosure; Stambhinī guards its opening, with the chariots and cavalry deliberately positioned.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Bhaṇḍa sends his sons with two hundred army divisions to capture Lalitā alive. Bālā, Lalitā’s daughter and perpetually nine-year-old martial prodigy, asks to fight as play despite her mother’s tenderness and concern.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Bālā persists; Lalitā embraces her, grants permission, armour and weapons, and a swan-drawn palanquin from her bow staff. Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā reluctantly guard her. The single Bālā appears separately to each prince and fights with missiles and countermissiles.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Bālā’s Nārāyaṇa missile burns the princes’ army. Thirty crescent-tipped arrows sever thirty heads simultaneously. Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā embrace her and report her success; Lalitā rejoices.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Bhaṇḍa grieves his sons and threatens personal revenge; his advisers restrain him. He sends invisible Viśukra to operate Jayavighna. Viśukra inscribes eight tridents and eight presiding powers on a stone slab, consecrates it with mantra and sacrifice, and throws it over the fire wall.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Jayavighna produces sleep, disengagement and rejection of the queen’s authority; the soldiers abandon weapons. Viśukra returns after midnight to exploit their apathy. Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā remain unaffected and report the unexplained breakdown to Lalitā.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Lalitā looks at Kāmeśvara and laughs; elephant-faced Gaṇanātha appears in her smile’s radiance, embraced by Siddhilakṣmī. He pulverizes Jayavighna with tusks, restoring readiness, then creates elephant-faced allies under six Vighnanāyakas.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Gaṇanātha’s forces destroy Viśukra’s troops. Viśukra sends Gajāsura, then flees as his strength declines. Mouse-mounted Gaṇeśvara kills Gajāsura and returns. Lalitā rewards him with precedence in worship before other deities.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Bhaṇḍa sends both brothers with Dhūminī’s nephews, whom he has trained. Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā leave a protective reserve. Duels pair Daṇḍanāthā with Viṣaṅga, Śyāmalā with Viśukra, and supporting commanders with nephews.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Viśukra’s Tṛṣāstra incapacitates the Śaktis with thirst. Mantriṇī proposes the ocean on Daṇḍanāthā’s chariot; at command Surāsindhu showers restoring drink. Śyāmalā surrounds her army with arrows to exclude asuras from it. Recovered troops prepare to resume.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Daṇḍanāthā rewards Surāsindhu with sacrificial use after mantra purification and benefits for worshippers. Battle resumes: the nephews die; Śyāmalā destroys Viśukra using Brahmaśiras. Daṇḍanāthā fights Viṣaṅga until midnight, hooks his head with her plough and kills him with an iron-club blow.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Grieving brothers and sons, Bhaṇḍa mobilizes his remaining commanders on Ābhila with Ghātaka sword. Lalitā undertakes the duel herself; Jvālāmālinī enlarges the camp exit. After the fourth morning’s army battle, Lalitā’s arrows multiply as they travel and strike.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Bhaṇḍa deploys darkness, heresy, blindness, power-loss, death, memory-loss, fear, disease and lost longevity; Lalitā successively counters each. Acyuta, Ananta and Govinda emerge from her three-name missile, burn diseases and receive a continuing healing charge.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Mahāsurāstra regenerates named asuras. Lalitā laughs; Durgā manifests with divine equipment and repeats the victories cited from Caṇḍikāsaptaśatī. Bhaṇḍa’s Mūkāstra meets Mahāvāgvādinī.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Veda-thieves are repelled from Lalitā’s right thumb nail. Her index-nail tortoise supports drowned Śaktis and drinks the flood; middle-nail boar destroys Hiraṇyākṣas. Ring-finger man-lion protects Prahlāda against eyebrow-born Hiraṇyakaśipus. Little-finger Vāmanas bind Balīndras.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Left-thumb Bhārgava Rāma kills Haihaya-generated Arjunas. Rāvaṇa emerges from Bhaṇḍa’s huṃkāra with Kumbhakarṇa and Meghanāda; left-index Kodaṇḍarāma and Lakṣmaṇa defeat them. Left-middle Tālāṅka defeats Dvivida’s monkeys; left-ring Viṣṇu’s Caturvyūha destroys Rājāsura kings.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Left-little-finger Kalki defeats Kali’s generated forces; the avatar leaders return to Vaikuṇṭha. Śāmbhava breaks Mahāmoha. Nārāyaṇa destroys the armies, Pāśupata the commanders, and Mahākāmeśvara kills Bhaṇḍa and burns Śūnyaka, including its women, children and stores. Lalitā brings exhausted troops back at sunset.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Lalitā’s healing gaze refreshes her army. Gods praise her cosmic forms, recall Kāma’s failed mission and present grief-stricken Rati, asking his revival to relieve her widowhood and enable Śiva’s marriage.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Lalitā restores Kāma from her glance. Śyāmalā adorns Rati; sages renew their marriage. Kāma offers service. Lalitā grants effective arrows, multiplied Kāmas and immunity from Śiva’s burning, directs punishment of devotee-tormentors through illicit desire, and fulfilment for respectful worshippers.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Kāma’s emanations spread; with Rati, Vasanta, moon and breeze he shoots Śiva, then Pārvatī. Mutual longing grows. Her father prescribes penance: winter immersion and summer fires under the sun. Śiva is pleased; formal marriage and residence at Kailāsa follow.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Śiva’s seed passes through Pārvatī, earth, fire, Kṛttikās and Gaṅgā to reeds; six-faced Mahāsena is born and nursed by Gaṅgā. His father trains him; he leads the gods, kills Tāraka and marries Indra’s daughter Devasenā. Kāma returns to serve Lalitā in Śrīpura.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Agastya asks what Śrīpura is; Hayagrīva recaps manifestation, marriage and Bhaṇḍa’s defeat. At Lalitā’s direction the triad commissions Viśvakarmā and Maya to construct sixteen residences. This starts a new city-description episode after the restored Kāma’s return.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly read accessible English witness; VERIFIED means witness check, not Sanskrit or cross-edition confirmation.

evidence.paraphrase: Mantriṇī dismantles Viśukra’s weapons and chariot equipment; Brahmaśiras destroys his body.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Daṇḍanāthā hooks Viṣaṅga’s head with the plough and kills him with the iron club after a long duel.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Daṇḍanāthā’s twelve-name series explicitly includes Vārāhī, Potriṇī and Vārtālī.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Śyāmalā’s name series explicitly includes Mantriṇī and other ministerial and musical names; the host calls them sixteen.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: The same elephant-faced figure appearing from Lalitā’s smile is subsequently named Gaṇanātha, Mahāgaṇapati and Gaṇeśvara.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Śrutavarmā states the sixty-thousand-year reign has expired and cannot be extended without worshipping Śiva; Bhīmakarmā counters with confidence in the existing half-strength battle power.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: In the gods’ retrospective speech, Brahmā performs mental, verbal and bodily penance; Viṣṇu grants ease of creation. Kāma manifests when Viṣṇu glances at Lakṣmī and receives weapons and victorious status.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: The gods report that Brahmā granted Tāraka boons and that only a son of Śiva is a feared opponent.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Viṣṇu creates Māyā to enchant Bhaṇḍa, grants concealed roaming and enjoyment; she requests and receives celestial assistants.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Lalitā promises benefits to those who devoutly recite the preceding hymn.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: The mobilization passage enumerates weapon varieties and diverse animal vehicles; only named weapon forms are indexed here.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Bhaṇḍa’s boast lists the following as his sons and adds that each has hundreds of sons. This is a claim in Bhaṇḍa’s speech, distinct from an independently narrated genealogy.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: The text announces thirty sons but its main list supplies twenty-two names; omitted names are not silently inserted from the translator’s footnote.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: The planned rear-attack command names fifteen assistants, with spelling differences later in the battle account.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: The numbered verses explicitly pair each harmful missile with Lalitā’s counter; weapon names are preserved without deriving historical equivalence.
evidence.verification_notes: Directly checked online English witness; Sanskrit and second-edition collation pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Rājāsura generates the listed demonic royal opponents; Lalitā’s left-ring-finger Viṣṇu forms Caturvyūha to defeat them.

boons_and_powers.austerity_or_circumstances: One hundred bows with Śatarudriya repetition taught by Citrakarmā; prolonged austerity not stated here.
boons_and_powers.requested: Half antagonist strength joins his own; his arrows nullify opponent missiles and weapons.
boons_and_powers.granted: Requests affirmed; sixty thousand years of kingship additionally granted.
boons_and_powers.mechanism: Opponent-strength transfer and hostile-weapon neutralization by arrows.
boons_and_powers.duration: Sixty thousand years explicitly qualifies rule; duration of combat powers is not separately specified.
boons_and_powers.notes: The sixty-thousand-year term is attached to kingship. Chapter12 counsel discusses its expiration while still invoking combat power. No inference that all powers expire or that Bhaṇḍa has an innate gender-based weakness.

boons_and_powers.requested: Rescue lives from Daitya harassment (verse31 marked defective in translation).
boons_and_powers.granted: Personal defeat of Bhaṇḍa and restoration of three worlds.
boons_and_powers.notes: Null fields are unstated in the cited examined passage unless otherwise noted; full corpus examination may add information.

boons_and_powers.austerity_or_circumstances: Seven brothers’ penance emaciates them; method and duration unstated.
boons_and_powers.requested: Sun inhabits their eyes in battle; sight burns and immobilizes enemies and weapons.
boons_and_powers.granted: Requested solar gaze power granted to all seven brothers.
boons_and_powers.mechanism: Sun in eyes acts on objects of their vision.
boons_and_powers.trigger: Seeing an antagonist while Sun is present in eyes.
boons_and_powers.counter: Andha blinds them; renewed solar presence is ineffective behind covered eyes, and weapon immobilization ends. This is demonstrated battle operation, not a separately stated grant restriction.
boons_and_powers.notes: One joint boon for the seven brothers; recipient_id is representative, shared_recipient_ids preserves all actual recipients.

boons_and_powers.mechanism: Fiery body encircles100yojanas, height30yojanas, leaving1yojana gate.

boons_and_powers.counter: Gaṇanātha pulverizes the slab and its presiding powers with his tusks.

boons_and_powers.austerity_or_circumstances: Long penance of mind, speech and body; narrated retrospectively by the gods.
boons_and_powers.requested: Create the whole mobile and immobile universe without strain through Viṣṇu’s grace.
boons_and_powers.granted: Brahmā described as having obtained his boon; burden of generation rests on Kāma.
boons_and_powers.notes: Creation-time flashback within narrative speech. Exact span of long penance unstated.

boons_and_powers.austerity_or_circumstances: Kāma’s manifestation in response to Viṣṇu’s glance at Lakṣmī.
boons_and_powers.granted: Invincibility and continuing victory; flowery arrows and sugarcane bow supplied.
boons_and_powers.notes: Chapter11 later narrates Śiva burning Kāma despite the gods’ recollection of victory promises. Retained without inventing an exception.

boons_and_powers.granted: A boon condition is reported: fear from Śiva’s son alone.
boons_and_powers.restrictions: Only Śiva’s son is named as feared antagonist.
boons_and_powers.notes: Austerity, request, duration and exact original grant are not narrated in this speech. Do not import another Purāṇa’s grantor.

boons_and_powers.austerity_or_circumstances: Created as a response to Bhaṇḍa’s strengthening and Indra’s decline.
boons_and_powers.requested: Celestial damsels to assist her task.
boons_and_powers.granted: Undetected roaming, enchantment and enjoyment; assistants supplied.
boons_and_powers.mechanism: Enchanting Bhaṇḍa and ministers through attraction and song.
boons_and_powers.notes: The grant precedes her request for assistants; request and initial grant are not interchangeable.

boons_and_powers.granted: Virtue, reputation, learning with humility, health, long life and family companionship.
boons_and_powers.trigger: Devout recitation of this chapter’s hymn.
boons_and_powers.notes: Future conditional blessing, distinct from Indra’s rescue request.

narrative_events.cause: Narrator introduces the adversary before Agastya asks how he arose.
narrative_events.details: Before the origin account, Hayagrīva previews Bhaṇḍa’s domination: Viśukra emerges from his right shoulder, Viṣaṅga from his left; he also creates sister Dūminī. The three oppose gods, who flee their offices and families.
narrative_events.outcome: Next chapter supplies origin and boons.
narrative_events.temporal_relation: PREVIEW: later reign narrated before chapter11 origin.

narrative_events.cause: Gods seek a son of Śiva to overcome Tāraka.
narrative_events.details: After Dākṣāyaṇī’s death, Śiva withdraws; her rebirth serves him. Gods oppressed by Tāraka seek a son of Śiva and send Kāma, recalling Viṣṇu’s earlier gifts. Kāma shoots Śiva, whose recovered composure leads him to burn Kāma with his third eye; Gaurī leaves for penance.
narrative_events.outcome: Kāma is burned; Gaurī begins penance.
narrative_events.temporal_relation: Includes creation-time retrospective speech (11.8–17) before return to Kāma mission.

narrative_events.cause: Citrakarmā acts on Kāma’s surviving ashes and teaches worship.
narrative_events.details: Citrakarmā shapes Kāma’s ashes into a boy; Rudra’s gaze animates him. Addressing him as son, Citrakarmā teaches Śatarudriya worship. Śiva accepts the boy’s requests for half his opponent’s strength and arrow-based neutralization of hostile weapons, additionally granting sixty thousand years of rule. Brahmā’s utterance supplies the name Bhaṇḍa.
narrative_events.outcome: Animated Bhaṇḍa obtains combat powers and a fixed royal term.

narrative_events.cause: Śukra organizes the new asura ruler’s accession.
narrative_events.details: Śukra crowns Bhaṇḍa; Maya rebuilds Śoṇitapura. Royal gifts include Vijaya bow, protective umbrella, disease-averting chowries and indestructible crown. Eight assistants and four wives are listed. The asuras maintain Vedic rites and Śiva worship during sixty thousand years.
narrative_events.outcome: Bhaṇḍa rules with assistants, wives, protections and religious observances.

narrative_events.cause: Viṣṇu observes growing asura strength; Nārada foresees danger after delusion ends.
narrative_events.details: Viṣṇu sends his deluding Māyā with Viśvācī’s companions; Bhaṇḍa neglects worship. Nārada urges Indra to worship Parāśakti. Śukra warns Bhaṇḍa; Śrutavarmā notes the expired reign, while Bhīmakarmā trusts his combat boon and urges disruption.
narrative_events.outcome: Indra worships Parāśakti; Bhaṇḍa chooses to disrupt worship despite warning about his royal term.
narrative_events.temporal_relation: Main progression after60k-year reign; ten-thousand-year delusion and later worship periods stated.

narrative_events.cause: Bhaṇḍa attacks divine worship and repeatedly fails against the wall.
narrative_events.details: Repeated attacks, including Vāyavya, fail against the regenerated divine wall. Indra’s gods offer their own flesh in a great sacrifice. Lalitā emerges with noose, goad, sugarcane bow and five arrows; her glance restores the mutilated gods.
narrative_events.outcome: Sacrificing gods receive Lalitā’s manifestation and bodily restoration.

narrative_events.cause: The restored gods surrender and Indra asks rescue.
narrative_events.details: The gods praise Lalitā’s cosmic identity; Indra requests rescue. She promises personally to defeat Bhaṇḍa and restore the worlds. Devout recitation of this hymn receives blessings of virtue, learning, longevity, health and family prosperity.
narrative_events.outcome: Lalitā promises victory over Bhaṇḍa and conditional hymn benefits.

narrative_events.cause: Brahmā considers coronation and a suitable divine spouse.
narrative_events.details: Gods and attendants arrive; Viśvakarmā builds a city at Brahmā’s command. Considering a suitable coronation and spouse, Brahmā sees Śiva assume a beautiful form and names him Kāmeśvara. Lalitā and Kāmeśvara mutually desire each other; Brahmā requests their joint enthronement.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva manifests as Kāmeśvara; mutual attraction prepares marriage.

narrative_events.cause: Lalitā sets independence as her marriage condition.
narrative_events.details: Lalitā insists on independence and a compatible husband; her thrown garland selects Kāmeśvara. Brahmā calls Viṣṇu her brother; Viṣṇu performs the marriage. Gods provide weapons and regalia. Brahmā’s Kusumākara chariot resists weapons, travels freely and removes afflictions through its fragrance.
narrative_events.outcome: She selects Kāmeśvara and receives ceremonial gifts at marriage.

narrative_events.cause: Nārada recalls the purpose of her manifestation after imperial festivities.
narrative_events.details: After the procession, Lalitā fulfills the assembly’s desires by her glance; Brahmā names her Kāmākṣī and Kāmeśvarī. Following ten thousand years of imperial life, Nārada recalls Bhaṇḍa’s threat. Gods return to their homes while continuing service through partial manifestations.
narrative_events.outcome: Gods return home while continuing partial service; the campaign follows.

narrative_events.cause: Lalitā resolves to conquer Bhaṇḍa.
narrative_events.details: Lalitā’s campaign begins. Sampatkarī emerges from her goad and leads elephants on Kaṇakolāhala. Atitvaritavikrānti emerges from the noose, rides Aparājita and leads cavalry; her four hands hold noose, goad, cane and bridle. Daṇḍanāthā’s war preparation follows.
narrative_events.outcome: Elephant and cavalry divisions emerge and set out.

narrative_events.cause: Daṇḍanāthā and Mantriṇī marshal their forces.
narrative_events.details: Daṇḍanāthā rides Vajraghoṣa with boar-faced troops. The text gives her twelve names, including Vārāhī, then Śyāmalā’s names, including Mantriṇī. Dhanurveda emerges from Śyāmalā’s parrot and gives Citrajīva and inexhaustible quivers. Yantriṇī and Tantriṇī attend her.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine names, vehicles and Śyāmalā’s bow establish their campaign roles.

narrative_events.cause: Campaign preparations reach the sovereign chariot.
narrative_events.details: Lalitā proceeds on Śrīcakra, armed with goad, noose, sugarcane bow and five arrows, attended by Kāmeśvarī and other eternal powers. Hayagrīva supplies twenty-five epithets and benefits of their recitation.
narrative_events.outcome: Lalitā advances with armed eternal attendants.

narrative_events.cause: Agastya requests the chariot gods’ names and weapons.
narrative_events.details: Hayagrīva describes Lalitā’s Cakrarāja tiers, including Siddhis, eight mothers, Mudrās, successive yoginī groups and fifteen Nityās. Mantriṇī’s seven-tier Geyacakra houses allied powers, Bhairavas, protective deities and guardians; petitions reach Lalitā through Mantriṇī. Alternative maternal iconography is explicitly reported.
narrative_events.outcome: The narrator enumerates deployment and Mantriṇī’s access role.

narrative_events.cause: Hayagrīva extends the army account to Daṇḍanāthā’s chariot.
narrative_events.details: Kiricakra houses Daṇḍanāthā and supporting powers, including Jṛmbhiṇī, Mohinī, Stambhinī, Dhātunāthās, personified plough and pestle, guardians and vehicles. Surāsindhu’s prospective role is to refresh thirsty combatants. The witness calls this a five-step chariot but later mentions a sixth step.
narrative_events.outcome: Kiricakra powers and support roles are introduced.

narrative_events.cause: Portents and the approaching campaign force Bhaṇḍa to deliberate.
narrative_events.details: Omens disturb Śūnyaka. Bhaṇḍa’s younger brothers Viśukra and Viṣaṅga advise him: Viśukra derides female opponents, while Viṣaṅga urges investigation and recalls earlier divine victories. Bhaṇḍa rejects the warning, boasts of his forces and named sons, and orders Kuṭilākṣa to fortify the city and send an advance force.
narrative_events.outcome: He dismisses caution and orders fortification and attack.

narrative_events.cause: Bhaṇḍa sends an initial general while protecting his city.
narrative_events.details: Bhaṇḍa sends Durmada; Kuṭilākṣa deploys Tālajaṅgha, Tālabhuja, Tālagrīva and Tālaketu at city gates. Sampatkarī fights Durmada on Raṇakolāhala. After Durmada strikes a crown jewel, her arrows pierce his chest and kill him; survivors flee.
narrative_events.outcome: Sampatkarī kills Durmada and survivors flee.

narrative_events.cause: Durmada’s elder brother seeks revenge.
narrative_events.details: Kuraṇḍa, Durmada’s elder brother, seeks revenge. The cavalry goddess asks Sampatkarī to yield the fight, then binds his army with multiplying nooses. Kuraṇḍa cuts her bowstring; she kills him with her goad, whose Pūtanās consume his forces. Survivors retreat.
narrative_events.outcome: The cavalry goddess kills Kuraṇḍa after the noose/bowstring exchange.

narrative_events.cause: Bhaṇḍa escalates after the two brothers’ defeat.
narrative_events.details: Five generals deploy Sarpiṇī, whose destroyed snakes multiply while she survives. Lalitā’s palate-born Nakulī rides Garuḍa, creates mongooses from her teeth and dissolves Sarpiṇī with Gāruḍa. Enemy arrows rout her mongooses; Akṣīṇanākula renews the force. Nakulī kills Karaṅka and four colleagues. Śyāmalā makes her a satellite deity; she spares surviving messengers.
narrative_events.outcome: Nakulī defeats regenerative snake magic and the five generals; survivors are released.

narrative_events.cause: Bhaṇḍa sends seven previously victorious solar-boon holders.
narrative_events.details: Kīkasā’s seven sons attack with a Sun-granted gaze that burns and immobilizes seen enemies and weapons. Lalitā summons Tiraskaraṇikā, Daṇḍanāthā’s guard. From Tamolipta she uses Mohana arrows and Andha to blind them; lost sight ends immobilization. She kills all seven, and the Śaktis destroy their army.
narrative_events.outcome: Tiraskaraṇikā’s blinding restores the Śaktis’ weapons; the generals die.
narrative_events.temporal_relation: Includes Sun-boon flashback at24.59–66 during narrated battle.

narrative_events.cause: Repeated frontal defeats prompt a concealed attack on the queen.
narrative_events.details: After defeats, Bhaṇḍa orders Viṣaṅga and fifteen generals to attack Lalitā’s rear secretly, aiming to destroy the source of her powers. Dark equipment and silence conceal their approach. They reach Cakrarāja’s ninth tier and wound defenders with invisible Vipāṭas.
narrative_events.outcome: The chariot’s lower defensive tier is penetrated.

narrative_events.cause: Two-sided pressure and a hit on royal equipment alarm the Nityās.
narrative_events.details: Kuṭilākṣa prevents the vanguard returning while Viṣaṅga breaks Lalitā’s fan. Nityās obtain her permission to intervene. Vahnivāsinī and Jvālāmālinī illuminate the attackers; the Nityās descend with Prāṇakodaṇḍas and fight for three watches.
narrative_events.outcome: Light removes concealment; direct fighting becomes possible.

narrative_events.cause: Illumination and Nityā counterattack reverse the ambush.
narrative_events.details: The Nityās kill the invading generals. Kāmeśvarī breaks Viṣaṅga’s armour; he escapes near dawn, destined for Daṇḍanāthā’s later attack. The Nityās refuse to pursue a fleeing warrior. Lalitā’s glance heals their wounds.
narrative_events.outcome: Viṣaṅga survives; wounded defenders are restored.

narrative_events.cause: The first night exposes a defensive failure.
narrative_events.details: Daṇḍanāthā routs Kuṭilākṣa’s night force. She and Mantriṇī acknowledge inadequate rear protection and propose a guarded fire enclosure. Lalitā approves defence before offence. Jvālāmālinī becomes the enclosure; Stambhinī guards its opening, with the chariots and cavalry deliberately positioned.
narrative_events.outcome: A fortified camp closes the route for another ordinary ambush.

narrative_events.cause: Fortification provokes a major assault; Bālā hears the princes approaching.
narrative_events.details: Bhaṇḍa sends his sons with two hundred army divisions to capture Lalitā alive. Bālā, Lalitā’s daughter and perpetually nine-year-old martial prodigy, asks to fight as play despite her mother’s tenderness and concern.
narrative_events.outcome: Mother and daughter debate permission to fight.

narrative_events.cause: Bālā’s resolve changes Lalitā’s initial refusal.
narrative_events.details: Bālā persists; Lalitā embraces her, grants permission, armour and weapons, and a swan-drawn palanquin from her bow staff. Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā reluctantly guard her. The single Bālā appears separately to each prince and fights with missiles and countermissiles.
narrative_events.outcome: Bālā enters with maternal equipment and protective escorts.

narrative_events.cause: Princes continue attacking after their army is destroyed.
narrative_events.details: Bālā’s Nārāyaṇa missile burns the princes’ army. Thirty crescent-tipped arrows sever thirty heads simultaneously. Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā embrace her and report her success; Lalitā rejoices.
narrative_events.outcome: All thirty princes die; their father’s grief initiates the next countermeasure.

narrative_events.cause: Loss of princes turns mourning into strategic revenge.
narrative_events.details: Bhaṇḍa grieves his sons and threatens personal revenge; his advisers restrain him. He sends invisible Viśukra to operate Jayavighna. Viśukra inscribes eight tridents and eight presiding powers on a stone slab, consecrates it with mantra and sacrifice, and throws it over the fire wall.
narrative_events.outcome: The consecrated enemy yantra enters the camp.

narrative_events.cause: Yantra’s influence demoralizes the rank and file.
narrative_events.details: Jayavighna produces sleep, disengagement and rejection of the queen’s authority; the soldiers abandon weapons. Viśukra returns after midnight to exploit their apathy. Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā remain unaffected and report the unexplained breakdown to Lalitā.
narrative_events.outcome: Unaffected commanders seek a remedy.

narrative_events.cause: Lalitā responds to commanders’ appeal.
narrative_events.details: Lalitā looks at Kāmeśvara and laughs; elephant-faced Gaṇanātha appears in her smile’s radiance, embraced by Siddhilakṣmī. He pulverizes Jayavighna with tusks, restoring readiness, then creates elephant-faced allies under six Vighnanāyakas.
narrative_events.outcome: Obstruction is removed and allied reinforcements emerge.

narrative_events.cause: Removal of the yantra permits the army to resume fighting.
narrative_events.details: Gaṇanātha’s forces destroy Viśukra’s troops. Viśukra sends Gajāsura, then flees as his strength declines. Mouse-mounted Gaṇeśvara kills Gajāsura and returns. Lalitā rewards him with precedence in worship before other deities.
narrative_events.outcome: Second night ends with victory and a ritual precedence boon.

narrative_events.cause: Viśukra’s prior defeat prompts a combined assault.
narrative_events.details: Bhaṇḍa sends both brothers with Dhūminī’s nephews, whom he has trained. Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā leave a protective reserve. Duels pair Daṇḍanāthā with Viṣaṅga, Śyāmalā with Viśukra, and supporting commanders with nephews.
narrative_events.outcome: Third day opens with paired battles.

narrative_events.cause: Asura army weakens, prompting a mass incapacitation weapon.
narrative_events.details: Viśukra’s Tṛṣāstra incapacitates the Śaktis with thirst. Mantriṇī proposes the ocean on Daṇḍanāthā’s chariot; at command Surāsindhu showers restoring drink. Śyāmalā surrounds her army with arrows to exclude asuras from it. Recovered troops prepare to resume.
narrative_events.outcome: Countermeasure restores strength without aiding the opposing army.

narrative_events.cause: Restored armies resume duels and overwhelm the combined force.
narrative_events.details: Daṇḍanāthā rewards Surāsindhu with sacrificial use after mantra purification and benefits for worshippers. Battle resumes: the nephews die; Śyāmalā destroys Viśukra using Brahmaśiras. Daṇḍanāthā fights Viṣaṅga until midnight, hooks his head with her plough and kills him with an iron-club blow.
narrative_events.outcome: Both Bhaṇḍa brothers die before the fourth day.

narrative_events.cause: Kin losses drive Bhaṇḍa into the final campaign.
narrative_events.details: Grieving brothers and sons, Bhaṇḍa mobilizes his remaining commanders on Ābhila with Ghātaka sword. Lalitā undertakes the duel herself; Jvālāmālinī enlarges the camp exit. After the fourth morning’s army battle, Lalitā’s arrows multiply as they travel and strike.
narrative_events.outcome: Lalitā and Bhaṇḍa enter a sustained missile exchange.

narrative_events.cause: Each harmful missile receives a specifically named opposing remedy.
narrative_events.details: Bhaṇḍa deploys darkness, heresy, blindness, power-loss, death, memory-loss, fear, disease and lost longevity; Lalitā successively counters each. Acyuta, Ananta and Govinda emerge from her three-name missile, burn diseases and receive a continuing healing charge.
narrative_events.outcome: Nine disabling powers are neutralized.

narrative_events.cause: Regenerated adversaries overpower the Śaktis, who seek Lalitā’s protection.
narrative_events.details: Mahāsurāstra regenerates named asuras. Lalitā laughs; Durgā manifests with divine equipment and repeats the victories cited from Caṇḍikāsaptaśatī. Bhaṇḍa’s Mūkāstra meets Mahāvāgvādinī.
narrative_events.outcome: Durgā destroys the manifested asuras and returns to Lalitā.

narrative_events.cause: Bhaṇḍa escalates to regenerated cosmic adversaries.
narrative_events.details: Veda-thieves are repelled from Lalitā’s right thumb nail. Her index-nail tortoise supports drowned Śaktis and drinks the flood; middle-nail boar destroys Hiraṇyākṣas. Ring-finger man-lion protects Prahlāda against eyebrow-born Hiraṇyakaśipus. Little-finger Vāmanas bind Balīndras.
narrative_events.outcome: Successive finger manifestations defeat the generated threats.

narrative_events.cause: Further generated armies continue the missile contest.
narrative_events.details: Left-thumb Bhārgava Rāma kills Haihaya-generated Arjunas. Rāvaṇa emerges from Bhaṇḍa’s huṃkāra with Kumbhakarṇa and Meghanāda; left-index Kodaṇḍarāma and Lakṣmaṇa defeat them. Left-middle Tālāṅka defeats Dvivida’s monkeys; left-ring Viṣṇu’s Caturvyūha destroys Rājāsura kings.
narrative_events.outcome: Generated epic and royal opponents are destroyed by corresponding manifestations.

narrative_events.cause: All successive countermeasures neutralize Bhaṇḍa’s supporting powers.
narrative_events.details: Left-little-finger Kalki defeats Kali’s generated forces; the avatar leaders return to Vaikuṇṭha. Śāmbhava breaks Mahāmoha. Nārāyaṇa destroys the armies, Pāśupata the commanders, and Mahākāmeśvara kills Bhaṇḍa and burns Śūnyaka, including its women, children and stores. Lalitā brings exhausted troops back at sunset.
narrative_events.outcome: Bhaṇḍa and capital are destroyed; the fourth day closes.

narrative_events.cause: Victory permits restoration of those affected by Kāma’s destruction.
narrative_events.details: Lalitā’s healing gaze refreshes her army. Gods praise her cosmic forms, recall Kāma’s failed mission and present grief-stricken Rati, asking his revival to relieve her widowhood and enable Śiva’s marriage.
narrative_events.outcome: Rati’s condition elicits the goddess’s compassion.

narrative_events.cause: Compassion for Rati prompts restoration; Kāma requests employment.
narrative_events.details: Lalitā restores Kāma from her glance. Śyāmalā adorns Rati; sages renew their marriage. Kāma offers service. Lalitā grants effective arrows, multiplied Kāmas and immunity from Śiva’s burning, directs punishment of devotee-tormentors through illicit desire, and fulfilment for respectful worshippers.
narrative_events.outcome: Restored Kāma receives protection and a mission.

narrative_events.cause: The newly protected love deity executes Lalitā’s commission.
narrative_events.details: Kāma’s emanations spread; with Rati, Vasanta, moon and breeze he shoots Śiva, then Pārvatī. Mutual longing grows. Her father prescribes penance: winter immersion and summer fires under the sun. Śiva is pleased; formal marriage and residence at Kailāsa follow.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva and Gaurī marry after her austerities.

narrative_events.cause: Marriage completes the divine rescue plan initiated in chapter11.
narrative_events.details: Śiva’s seed passes through Pārvatī, earth, fire, Kṛttikās and Gaṅgā to reeds; six-faced Mahāsena is born and nursed by Gaṅgā. His father trains him; he leads the gods, kills Tāraka and marries Indra’s daughter Devasenā. Kāma returns to serve Lalitā in Śrīpura.
narrative_events.outcome: Tāraka’s defeat closes the origin-to-restoration chain; Kāma returns to Lalitā.

narrative_events.cause: Question arising from Śrīpura’s mention at30.107.
narrative_events.details: Agastya asks what Śrīpura is; Hayagrīva recaps manifestation, marriage and Bhaṇḍa’s defeat. At Lalitā’s direction the triad commissions Viśvakarmā and Maya to construct sixteen residences. This starts a new city-description episode after the restored Kāma’s return.
narrative_events.outcome: Boundary confirmed: war/restoration narrative has ended; capital description begins.

Online chapter29 includes an unnumbered premature death synopsis after93 while numbered94–138 continue the fight; numbered139–144 establish the final death sequence. Treat as online-witness sequencing issue until scan collation.

Witness alternates Kaṇakolāhala/Raṇakolāhala for Sampatkarī’s elephant; Kālavāśita/Kākavāśita and Vajradanta/Vijradanta in general lists; Dūminī/Dhūminī; multiple rear-attack names. These have not been automatically collapsed into unique people or reconciled by memory.
Chapter17.33–35 calls the name series sixteen but the displayed series supplies fifteen recognizable entries. Sanskrit or scan check required. No sixteenth name invented.

Chariot lists contain Gariraā, repeated Hākinī and Siddhalakṣmī, six Guptatarā entries, and a fifth-tier sixteen-deity heading whose displayed enumeration is ambiguous. These literal names are contextualized and queued for Sanskrit/scan resolution. No expansion from later standard Śrīcakra lists.

Chapter16 names the noose-born cavalry leader Atitvaritavikrānti; chapter22 names its Aparājita-mounted combatant Caṇḍī, Turagānanā and Hayāsanā, while chapter28 names Aśvārūḍhā. Role and vehicle continuity suggest identification, but these local records are not automatically merged before Sanskrit collation.
